title: Compatibility Mode & Shim Generator: runtime opt-in flags and safe rollout gates
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: We need a predictable, low-risk path to introduce breaking runtime changes while preserving customer uptime and minimizing integration work. Current approach (deprecation windows + doc notices) is insufficient for server-side runtime changes that alter tokenization, KV cache semantics, or wire-level protocol behavior. Goal: define a runtime-level 'compatibility mode' mechanism, implement a shim-generator that produces adapters for older client contracts, and wire those into rollout gates so breaking changes can be safely staged and reverted.
acceptance_criteria: Spec for compatibility-mode flags published in Confluence with migration timelines and behavioral matrix
Shim-generator CLI prototype that takes a runtime JSON contract diff and emits an adapter binary or config mapping
Server-side support for per-customer "compat_mode" flag that alters kernel selection and KV cache semantics behind a stable toggle
Rollout pipeline integrated with canary groups + automatic rollback on regression signals (latency or quality thresholds)
Docs and an RFC explaining when to use compatibility mode vs breaking release, and how long deprecation windows must be
Telemetry events emitted for toggles, shim usage, and migration-assistant outcomes
notes: 2026-03-02: Initial scoping meeting with Runtime, Client SDK, and Product. Decision: prefer server-side compatibility flags to avoid forcing every customer SDK update for a single breaking kernel change.

2026-03-03: Trade-off: compatibility flags increase maintenance surface (supporting two execution paths) but reduce customer outages. We recommend an automated deprecation timeline of 6 months for non-security breaking changes and 30 days for security fixes.

2026-03-04: Rajan to prototype shim-generator that converts old request/response shapes to new ones using a declarative mapping language. Prototype target: model input tokenization differences and 'option renames' transformations.

2026-03-05: PM feedback (Sofia Martinez): require a migration-assistant CLI that validates a customer's critical prompt set against new runtime behavior and reports quality regressions before flipping the toggle. Add to scope.
2026-03-06: Design review notes: DES-118 proposed a UX for Console toggles per-customer; link to mockups: https://drive.redwood.com/designs/compat-mode-console-mockup.png

2026-03-08: Security: flagged that shim-generator binaries must be signed and provenance logged. Security team (Elena Park) requested threat model doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/x/CompatShimThreatModel
2026-03-09: Engineering review (runtime-core): kernel-selection needs an extension point for compatibility predicates. Reference PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123 (WIP)

2026-03-10: Stakeholder alignment: launch plan for runtime-2.0 will gate any breaking change with an opt-in compatibility flag + shim availability. If shim is not feasible, require canary group and extended deprecation window. Logged follow-ups: ENG-99902 (shim-generator followups), ENG-99903 (console UX implementation)
